title: Prove the sharp P104 joint rerouting cost after releasing both private legs
body:
Retiring either chart-278 exterior port and releasing **both** private transfers through chart 288 has minimum replacement tariff **$L[p(7)+p(2)+p(5)]$** on $L$ independent copies of Clear1nsight's #7786 rational word. The optimum allows arbitrary fixed finite routes on the 1,103 chart labels and scalar rational-linear coding across copies, with the other native paid values fixed. Deterministic receiver readouts may be nonlinear.

Two independent input coordinates force two disjoint scalar paths per copy. A separate three-coordinate witness requires an exit from a set of charts whose only member in the source-to-receiver interval is 288. Combining the two constraints determines the optimum even for longer paths, feedback and joint coding. Its unique paid topology consists of the direct 278 → 127 transfer and the two private legs 278 → 288 → 127, each repeated $L$ times. For one copy **9,275** distinct feasible edge multisets attain total grade fourteen. Eight chronological programs were checked against all 1,289 output operators.

After crediting all three removed transfers, the cheaper exterior retirement still adds **94.9667971064257… paid units** on the enrolled 48-call invoice. The joint theorem assumes independent copies. The invoice compares 48 separately instantiated calls. This resolves the private-route question from #7818 and leaves the selected conditional exponent at 0.00363005817.

Clear1nsight supplied the word and the side-input witness in #7786 and #7795, building on Ali Romman's #7776 caller. The previous single-route and fixed-private-slot studies are #7808 and #7818.

All 8 registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and in a read-only, Git-free export of the submitted commit. The source-history, committed-byte, mode and export-inventory checks passed.
